task: Remediate the source-map-js high-severity dependency vulnerability by pinning the transitive dependency to 1.2.2 while preserving dependency manifest authority and existing runtime behavior.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: A current high-severity npm advisory blocks every release. The patch is a transitive dependency update, but it affects the locked install contract and therefore must remain deterministic, exact-version pinned, Atlas-resolved and proven by the real npm audit rather than an exception.

acceptanceCriteria: Root dependency manifests remain canonically classified as DOMAIN-RELEASE.
package.json explicitly overrides source-map-js to exactly 1.2.2.
package-lock.json resolves node_modules/source-map-js to version 1.2.2 with the matching registry artifact and integrity.
PostCSS remains on the existing 8.5.28 contract and continues to consume a compatible source-map-js version.
The real CI security-audit job no longer reports GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q / the source-map-js 1.2.1 high-severity finding.
Quality, TypeScript and production build remain green; no product runtime/auth/AAL2 behavior is changed.
invariants: Security audit is not disabled, downgraded, allowlisted or bypassed.
The fix uses the patched dependency version rather than suppressing npm audit output.
No unrelated dependency is intentionally upgraded.
The lockfile remains deterministic and compatible with npm ci.
The package authority classification proven in the first coherent batch remains intact.

failureModes: Only package.json is changed and package-lock.json continues installing vulnerable 1.2.1.
Only the lockfile is changed and a future lock regeneration falls back to a vulnerable transitive version.
An audit ignore/allowlist makes CI green without removing the vulnerable package.
The override uses a loose range and later resolves to an unreviewed version.
The lockfile integrity/resolved tuple does not match 1.2.2 and npm ci fails.
The dependency fix triggers unrelated transitive package churn.
Package manifests regress to unresolved Atlas ownership.
edgeCases: source-map-js is transitive rather than a direct runtime dependency.
The newly published 1.2.2 package must be pinned exactly despite the parent range.
Security proof is accepted only from the actual exact-head security-audit job, not from source assertions alone.

alternatives.summary: Suppress or allowlist the new npm audit advisory.
alternatives.reason: That weakens the security gate and leaves the vulnerable package installed.

alternatives.summary: Upgrade PostCSS or broader dependency groups to chase the transitive dependency.
alternatives.reason: PostCSS already allows the patched source-map-js patch; broader churn is unnecessary.

alternatives.summary: Add an exact source-map-js 1.2.2 root override and update only its lock entry.
alternatives.reason: This is the smallest deterministic remediation compatible with the existing PostCSS contract.

specialistReviews.finding: Exact-head npm audit reports a high-severity source-map-js 1.2.1 vulnerability.
specialistReviews.resolution: Replace the installed transitive package with patched 1.2.2; no audit exception is permitted.

specialistReviews.finding: Dependency manifests are now explicitly owned by DOMAIN-RELEASE and may be safely included in the planned projection.
specialistReviews.resolution: Retain exact release-domain ownership and its Atlas regression.

specialistReviews.finding: A broad npm update could change unrelated dependency truth.
specialistReviews.resolution: Pin exactly 1.2.2 and change only the source-map-js lock entry plus the explicit override.

challenge.scenario: The audit is silenced without changing the package.
challenge.finding: CI could turn green while the vulnerable code remains.
challenge.resolution: No audit configuration changes are in scope; exact-head npm audit must pass naturally.

challenge.finding: Future regeneration could select another vulnerable version allowed by the parent range.
npm ci requires the locked install graph to agree.
challenge.resolution: Update the source-map-js lock entry to 1.2.2 as the same coherent batch.

challenge.scenario: npm update changes unrelated transitive packages.
challenge.finding: Security remediation becomes an unbounded dependency release.
challenge.resolution: Do not regenerate the full graph; modify only the exact transitive lock record required by the override.
PostCSS 8.5.28 declares ^1.2.1, which includes 1.2.2; full tests/build remain mandatory.

challenge.finding: npm ci fails or artifact identity is unproven.
challenge.resolution: Use the published 1.2.2 registry URL and package integrity and prove through npm ci in CI.

challenge.scenario: The package files lose domain classification.
challenge.finding: A future dependency security edit becomes semantically unresolved again.
challenge.resolution: Keep the exact DOMAIN-RELEASE classification regression in the final release.

proofPlan: Run Plan Before Code again on this expanded exact-head plan before editing package.json or package-lock.json.
Add exact root override source-map-js=1.2.2 and update only the source-map-js lock record.
Add a deterministic dependency-security contract test asserting the override and locked 1.2.2 artifact.
Run Edit-Time and full Incremental Known Failure Replay.
Require Release Risk Budget PASS for the combined quality-infrastructure plus dependency-contract release diff.
Require the exact-head security-audit job to PASS with no audit exception.
Run full Quality Tests, TypeScript and Production Build, then Completion Truth and lifecycle closure.

requirements.requirement: The locked dependency contract installs source-map-js 1.2.2 instead of vulnerable 1.2.1 without weakening audit enforcement or changing product runtime behavior.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: The security remediation must not disable, suppress or allowlist the npm audit finding.
The lockfile must not retain source-map-js 1.2.1.
The remediation must not intentionally upgrade unrelated dependencies.

requirements.requirement: The dependency security remediation stays within the canonical release risk budget and preserves release-domain manifest ownership.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: The security release must not expand into unrelated product or dependency subsystems.

notes: A new high-severity npm advisory surfaced after the E13 quality release had already reached Completion Truth. Main currently locks source-map-js 1.2.1 through PostCSS 8.5.28 (^1.2.1). The first coherent batch on this branch established exact DOMAIN-RELEASE ownership for package.json/package-lock.json and passed Plan Before Code, Edit-Time and full Replay. This expanded plan now authorizes only the patched 1.2.2 dependency remediation; security-audit remains fully enforced.
